text:
Anika: CI red on macOS-latest for the new scheduler handshake test. Fails ~1/40 locally on my M1. Error: 'handshake timeout after 200ms' in test_scheduler_handshake. Anyone seen this?

Chris: saw a couple in the last 24h. Timing-sensitive when worker spawn overlaps with ack. Repro steps?

Anika: run with RUST_LOG=trace and `cargo test test_scheduler_handshake -- --nocapture` — here's the failing snippet I get:

```
[WARN] handshake timeout for worker id=7 seq=42 elapsed=210ms
thread 'test_scheduler_handshake' panicked at 'assert_eq! expected Ok, got Err', tests/scheduler.rs:120
```

Mike: can you try single-threaded test runner: `cargo test -- --test-threads=1`? Suspect a race between spawn and ack handlers.

Anika: tried that, still flaky. Mac: ~1/25, Linux: consistently green.

Sam: if we need to bisect, what's the last green commit for that job? @ci-bot can you check?

ci-bot: last green for job/scheduler-unit on macOS-latest: 1759987654. Re-run requested: https://ci.internal/retry/1761112223

Jen: quick mitigation: add deterministic seed to test scheduler RNG and relax timeout for macos to 500ms. Also print detailed handshake trace on failure.

Chris: +1 on seed. Also add a small retry wrapper in the test harness (try up to 3 times) so transient flakes don't block merges while we root cause. Make sure we still surface logs on final failure.

Anika: I'll open a tiny PR with: deterministic seed, timeout bump, and retry logic. Assigning to @Chris for review.

Mike: If you want faster triage, include the minimal repro (single test binary) and `--exact` flag in the PR description.

Anika: good call. Will include `cargo test test_scheduler_handshake -- --exact --nocapture` and a link to the CI job. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Chris: also add a short note in the test header referencing this thread so future devs know it's timing-sensitive.

Anika: done, PR opened: https://phabricator.internal/D1234 — pinging @Chris for review.

Jen: :shipit: once CI is stable, we can follow up with a deeper root-cause (scheduler start ordering) investigation.

Sam: If bisect becomes necessary, I'll volunteer to run the binary-level bisection across the last 200 commits.

Anika: great, thanks everyone. We'll iterate after the tiny fix lands.
